item.title: Animal Crossing Is Finally Getting Some Real Competition With Petit Planet for Switch 2 In 2027
item.description: Many Animal Crossing competitors have emerged since New Horizons became a breakout success in 2020 , but few have a chance to take on the popular Nintendo series like HoYoverse's Petit Planet . Now, we've learned that a showdown between the two games will take place on Nintendo Switch 2, as a release window for a port was recently confirmed.

item.title: The 10 Most Anticipated Sci-Fi and Fantasy Books of November 2026
item.description: When fall brings cold, windy, and wet weather, it’s the perfect time to stay inside and curl up with a good book. November offers plenty of options, with fresh entries in long-running series, standalones by bestselling authors, and brand-new talent to check out. Whether you want to imagine sailing with sky pirates, exploring a haunted forest, or flirting with faeries, the 10 most anticipated sci-fi and fantasy books of November offer plenty of ways to pass a rainy day.

item.title: 15 Years Ago, Zelda Told its Most Memorable Story with its Worst Gameplay
item.description: Hold the controller over your head. The Master Sword glows. Point it at the screen, hit Y to recenter, and swing. On the screen, Link swings… kind of the right way. Then, your chatty companion, Fi, chimes in with a very long and earnest explanation of something you figured out several minutes ago. Rinse and repeat for about 40 hours, and that’s Skyward Sword , one of the most cinematic, heartrending, memorable stories Zelda has ever told — and the one saddled with the most finicky gameplay.

item.title: Dungeons & Dragons Turned Hansel and Gretel Into a Near-Perfect Adventure
item.description: Most of the published adventures for Dungeons & Dragons focus on epic fantasy , tasking players with fighting ancient necromancers, rampaging demons, or invading armies in order to prevent some great calamity. But the stakes don’t have to be so high to have a great session, and a bit of whimsy can prove just as memorable as a dramatic battle. That’s why one of my favorite adventures from Wizards of the Coast is a silly fairy tale inspired by Hansel and Gretel.

item.title: Netflix's Near-Perfect Thriller With 94% Rotten Tomatoes Score Is Getting Cut From Streaming
item.description: The End of the F***ing World is among the best in this genre. Based on Charles Forsman’s minicomics, the eight-part miniseries follows James (Alex Lawther), a teen who thinks he is a psychopath, and Alyssa (Jessica Barden), who considers James a welcome distraction from her tumultuous home life.

item.title: 7 Near-Perfect Prime Video Sci-Fi Shows that Hook You in the First Scene
item.description: Prime Video is home to sci-fi shows of great variety, but some of the best ones capture our attention from the get-go. When a premise is solid and well-thought-out, the first episode often becomes a promising indicator for the rest of the story. With that in mind, here are seven near-perfect Prime Video sci-fi shows that hook you right from the first scene.

item.title: 6 Perfect 'Peanuts' Comics from the 1960s that Prove Charles Schulz is a Genius
item.description: By the 1960s, Schulz hit his sweet spot with well-defined characters and a freshness to the material which would sometimes flag in the decades to come. Don’t get me wrong, there are plenty of hilarious, heartwarming, and inspired Peanuts comics from the ‘70s, ‘80s, and ‘90s, but taken as a whole, nothing tops 1960s Peanuts .

item.title: Welcome to the New Era of Video Game Adaptations
item.description: Buckle up, because that trend is about to kick into full gear. This week, we got a flood of news stories confirming that Hollywood is in a full-on gold rush. The film rights to video games are currently getting snapped up at an alarming rate. While that’s not exactly new for an industry that has a long history of eyeing game movies that never pass the scripting phase, we’re actually seeing significant developments that signal an approaching tidal wave.

item.title: 20 Years Later, The Departed's Best Line Is Still One Of The Greatest Quotes In Gangster Movie History
item.description: In crime cinema, a lethal line of dialogue can carry just as much weight as a loaded gun. Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas hooks audiences with Henry Hill's seductive declaration, “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster,” framing a life of crime as the ultimate aspiration. Miller's Crossing features Tom Reagan's wonderfully blunt take on underworld survival, while Casino , Scarface , and The Godfather overflow with dialogue that has long since bled into the cultural lexicon. Immortal phrases like “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer” and “an offer you can’t refuse” remain cinematic icons right alongside the actors and directors who brought them to life.

item.title: Forget Jason Statham, the Best Action Movie of the Last 30 Years Is Back on Netflix
item.description: Harrison Ford spent decades making wildly implausible heroes feel like ordinary guys having a terrible day. An archaeologist outrunning a giant boulder? Sure. A space smuggler taking on an evil empire? Absolutely. In Air Force One , he pulls off something that now feels considerably more farfetched: an American president you’d trust with your life.
